summary:
Chandrayantra is a physics\-guided, AI\-assisted decision\-support system developed to detect and characterize subsurface ice in the Moon's south polar region using Chandrayaan\-2 DFSAR radar and OHRC imagery data. The project addresses the challenge of accurately distinguishing ice deposits from rocky lunar terrain, a limitation of conventional radar\-based detection methods.

Our solution integrates radar, optical, terrain, and illumination data to generate confidence\-based ice maps, estimate subsurface ice volume, identify safe landing zones, and optimize rover traversal paths. By combining advanced geospatial analysis, machine learning, and mission\-planning algorithms, Chandrayantra transforms raw lunar data into actionable insights for future exploration missions.

The project is important because lunar ice can serve as a critical resource for water, oxygen, and fuel production, enabling sustainable human presence on the Moon. By improving ice detection accuracy and supporting mission planning, Chandrayantra helps reduce exploration risks and contributes to the future of lunar exploration and habitation.
details:
Project Details – Chandrayantra

Chandrayantra is a physics-guided, AI-assisted lunar exploration framework developed to detect, characterize, and utilise subsurface ice deposits in the Moon's south polar region. The system processes Chandrayaan-2 DFSAR radar data together with OHRC imagery, terrain information, and illumination data to identify high-confidence ice-bearing regions. It then extends beyond ice detection by recommending safe landing zones, planning efficient rover traverses, and estimating subsurface ice volume for future lunar missions.

How It Works

  1. Collects and processes Chandrayaan-2 DFSAR radar and OHRC imagery data.
  2. Extracts radar backscatter, CPR, DOP, terrain, and illumination features.
  3. Uses a physics-guided AI approach to differentiate subsurface ice from rocky terrain and reduce false detections.
  4. Generates confidence-based ice probability maps.
  5. Identifies safe landing sites near potential ice deposits.
  6. Calculates optimal rover paths using path-planning algorithms.
  7. Estimates the volume and distribution of subsurface ice deposits.

Benefits

  • More accurate subsurface ice detection.
  • Reduced false positives caused by rough lunar terrain.
  • Safer landing site selection.
  • Optimised rover navigation with lower operational risk.
  • Estimation of accessible lunar resources for future missions.
  • End-to-end support from detection to mission planning.

Intended Impact

The project supports future lunar exploration by helping scientists and mission planners locate and utilise water-ice resources. Lunar ice can potentially provide water, oxygen, and rocket fuel, making long-term human presence on the Moon more sustainable. By improving mission safety and resource assessment, Chandrayantra contributes to the development of future lunar bases and exploration programmes.

Technologies, Tools and Software Used

  • IDAS (Modular Inversion and Data Analysis System) for DFSAR radar calibration and backscatter extraction.
  • Python with NumPy, SciPy, and OpenCV for data processing and image analysis.
  • GDAL and Rasterio for geospatial raster processing.
  • QGIS / ArcGIS for spatial visualisation and terrain analysis.
  • MATLAB / Python for dielectric and ice-volume modelling.
  • NetworkX for A* and D* Lite rover path-planning algorithms.

Creativity and Innovation

What makes Chandrayantra unique is that it goes beyond creating ice-detection maps. The project combines physics-based modelling, artificial intelligence, geospatial analysis, and mission-planning techniques into a single framework. Instead of providing binary ice/no-ice predictions, it generates confidence-based assessments and converts scientific data into actionable decisions for landing and exploration missions.

Key Factors Considered

  • Accuracy of subsurface ice detection.
  • Reduction of radar-based false positives.
  • Terrain hazards and slope conditions.
  • Illumination and solar power availability.
  • Landing safety requirements.
  • Rover energy efficiency and traversal risk.
  • Resource estimation for future lunar exploration.
